skill.description: Generate, review, and validate Git commit messages using Conventional Commits with optional GitHub issue context.
skill.summary: Commit message guidance, history review, and issue-aware commit support for Git workflows.
skill.author: C0ntr0lledCha0s

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown examples or expected git and GitHub CLI subprocess calls without shell interpolation. One real filesystem issue remains: a predictable /tmp commit-message file can be replaced or clobbered, and the issue cache stores GitHub issue body previews locally.

remediation.suggestion: Replace /tmp/commit-msg.txt with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile or pass the message through a securely created temporary file that is removed after use.

remediation.issue: GitHub issue body previews are cached on disk
remediation.suggestion: Do not request issue body content by default, or make body-preview caching opt in with clear retention and cleanup behavior.

remediation.issue: External git and gh commands run from helper scripts
remediation.suggestion: Document that the skill executes local git commands and GitHub CLI reads, and keep all subprocess calls shell-free with fixed command allowlists.

content.user_title: Manage Git Commits with Issue Context
content.value_statement: Inconsistent commit messages make review, changelogs, and automation harder. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code create, review, and validate Conventional Commits with GitHub issue context.
actual_capabilities: Suggests Conventional Commit types, scopes, subjects, bodies, and footers.
Reviews recent commit history for format, clarity, size, and issue references.
Analyzes staged or changed files to group related work into logical commits.
Uses GitHub issue cache data to suggest Closes or Refs footers.
Provides examples for breaking changes, co-authors, reverts, and changelog-ready commits.
limitations: Requires a Git repository for history and diff analysis.
GitHub issue integration depends on the GitHub CLI and local authentication.
Generated messages still need human review before committing.
It cannot guarantee that a commit is atomic without understanding project intent.

use_cases.title: Write a clear commit message
use_cases.description: Generate a concise Conventional Commit message from staged changes and add issue references when appropriate.

use_cases.title: Review branch history before a pull request
use_cases.description: Check recent commits for format problems, vague subjects, large changes, and missing issue links.

use_cases.title: Standardize team release notes
use_cases.description: Apply consistent commit types and breaking-change footers so changelog automation has reliable input.

prompt_templates.title: Suggest a commit message
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me write a Conventional Commit message for my staged changes.

prompt_templates.title: Review my commits
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the commits on my current branch for Conventional Commit format, clarity, and issue references.

prompt_templates.title: Split work into commits
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze my changed files and suggest logical commit groups with commit messages for each group.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare release-ready history
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit my branch history for changelog quality, breaking-change notation, issue references, and commits that should be squashed.

output_examples.input: Help me write a commit message for staged auth changes.
output_examples.output: A suggested Conventional Commit with type, scope, short subject, explanatory body, and an optional Closes footer.

output_examples.input: Review my recent commits before I open a pull request.
output: A compliance summary for recent commit subjects.
Specific suggestions for vague messages, missing issue references, and oversized commits.

output_examples.input: Group my changed files into atomic commits.
output_examples.output: A set of logical commit groups with proposed scopes and user-editable commit messages.

best_practices: Stage only one logical change before asking for a final commit message.
Review generated issue footers before committing, especially Closes references.
Use breaking-change footers when a change requires user migration.
anti_patterns: Do not use generated commit text without checking the diff yourself.
Do not close issues from a commit unless the change fully resolves them.
Do not combine unrelated feature, fix, test, and documentation changes in one commit.

faq.question: Does this skill create commits automatically?
faq.answer: It can support commit creation workflows, but users should review the staged changes and final message before committing.

faq.question: Does it require Conventional Commits?
faq.answer: The skill is built around Conventional Commits, but it can also explain quality issues in ordinary Git messages.

faq.question: Can it link commits to GitHub issues?
faq.answer: Yes. It can use branch names and cached GitHub issue data to suggest Closes or Refs footers.

faq.question: Can it analyze commit history?
faq.answer: Yes. It can inspect recent commits for message format, clarity, size, and potential squash opportunities.

faq.question: Does it send data to GitHub?
faq.answer: Some helper scripts use the GitHub CLI to read repository and issue information when issue integration is used.

faq.question: Is it useful for teams?
faq.answer: Yes. It helps teams keep commit history consistent for review, changelog generation, and release automation.
